name: Thyme

companions.note: Thyme repels cabbage worms and whiteflies; excellent brassica companion
Same cabbage pest deterrence as with kale
Thyme repels aphids and hornworms; both thrive in full sun
Both attract beneficial insects; good pollinator corridor together

pnw_notes: One of the most reliably perennial herbs in zone 8b — stays evergreen through Portland winters. Harvest sprigs year-round; flavor peaks just before flowering in late spring. Needs excellent drainage; raised beds are ideal. Trim back by one third after bloom to keep bushy. English thyme (T. vulgaris) has the classic savory flavor; Lemon thyme (T. citriodorus) adds bright citrus notes — both care the same. Great with roasted root vegetables and brassicas.

frost_hardiness.notes: Evergreen in zone 8b — keeps harvestable leaves all winter. Woodier stems protect the crown through freezes.

planting_windows.notes: Spring transplant; establish before summer heat
Fall transplant works well — roots establish in cool soil; harvest lightly until spring
Year-round harvest; peak flavor May–September just before and during bloom
